privacyPageIntro1: This privacy notice tells you what to expect us to do with your personal information when we collect it within and in relation to the Fish Export Service (FES).
privacyPageIntro2: For the purposes of this Privacy Notice, “we” means Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), Marine Management Organisation (<abbr title='Marine Management Organisation'>MMO</abbr>) and other UK Marine Fisheries authorities operating in the UK which at the current time includes Marine Directorate (Scotland), Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs - Northern Ireland (DAERA), Welsh Government (WG), Department of Environment, Food and Agriculture – Isle of Man (DEFA), Government of Jersey, The States of Guernsey.
privacyPageIntro3: The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) collects your personal information and is the data processor for the personal information you provide.
privacyPageDataControllersIntro: The data controllers are MMO and the other UK Marine Fisheries authorities operating in the UK:
privacyPageDataControllersLi3: Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (Northern Ireland)
privacyPageDataControllersLi4: Department of Environment, Food and Agriculture (Isle of Man)
privacyPagePurposeHeading: Purpose for processing – why we are collecting your personal data
privacyPagePurposeDesc1: We collect and process your personal information so you can be issued a UK export catch certificate, processing statement or non-manipulation document, by accessing the service operated by Defra and processed by the Marine Management Organisation (MMO) and other UK Marine Fisheries authorities operating in the UK (as listed above).
privacyPagePurposeDesc2: We will also process FES data for purposes including compliance with legal obligations, archiving purposes, scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes.
privacyPagePurposeDesc3: MMO generates yearly statistics providing a broad picture of the UK fishing industry and its operations. Our publications includes data on the structure, activity and landings of the UK fleet alongside additional information on overseas trade, exploitation of stocks and the world fishing industry.
privacyPagePurposeDesc4: We also use your personal information with Google Analytics & Microsoft Clarity to monitor your online progress through the service, helping us to improve your experience.
privacyPagePurposeDesc5: We partner with Microsoft Clarity and Microsoft Advertising to capture how you use and interact with our website through behavioural metrics, heatmaps, and session replay to improve and market our products/services. Website usage data is captured using first and third-party cookies and other tracking technologies to determine the popularity of products/services and online activity. Additionally, we use this information for site optimization, fraud/security purposes, and advertising.
privacyPagePurposeDesc6Prefix: For more information about how Microsoft collects and uses your data, visit the
privacyPagePurposeDesc7: We do not track IP address or individual User IDs in Google Analytics.

privacyPageObtainedHeading: How your personal data has been obtained
privacyPageObtainedDesc: In addition to information we obtain from you directly, such as via forms that you have submitted to us, some information is obtained indirectly via:
privacyPageObtainedLi1: Your Government Gateway or GOV UK One Login account
privacyPageObtainedLi3: Data supplied by agents or other third party representatives on your behalf
privacyPageLawfulBasisHeading: Why we are able to process your personal data
privacyPageLawfulBasisDesc1: The lawful basis for processing your data is to allow the Fish Export Service to generate the required documents for the customer to support accurate submissions to facilitate trade. It is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest, which is laid down by law, or in the exercise of official authority vested in the data controller.
privacyPageLawfulBasisDesc2: Furthermore, where such data relates to the possibility of a criminal offence, this data is further processed under Part 3 of the Data Protection Act 2018 (“The Act”) which states that competent authorities may process personal data for law enforcement purposes, as defined under Section 31 of the Act.
privacyPageLawfulBasisDesc3: Section 31 of the Act defines law enforcement purposes as “the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties, including the safeguarding against, and the prevention of threats to public security”.
privacyPageLawfulBasisDesc4: The Marine Management Organisation is a competent authority as referred to in Part 3 of the Act where its statutory functions are set out in the Marine & Coastal Access Act 2009, the Fisheries Act 2020 and associated legislation as referred to in those Acts.
privacyPageConsentHeading: Consent to process your personal data
privacyPageConsentDesc: The processing of your personal data is not based on consent. You cannot withdraw it.
privacyPageSharingHeading: Who we share your personal data with
privacyPageSharingDesc1: We will share personal information with other partners, for example other UK Fishing Authorities, where this is necessary to pursue a task in the public interest or official function of a public body. This includes where there is a clear basis in law or where, for example, sharing helps to fulfil MMOs functions or those of another government Department such as Defra.
privacyPageSharingDesc2: We will share catch certificates, processing statements and non-manipulation documents with the EU’s CATCH system. CATCH is the European Union (EU) database for the management of catch certificates and documents that must be provided by EU importers and Member State competent authorities to demonstrate that illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing has not taken place.
privacyPageSharingDesc3: Where required by law, data may be published on UK Government or EU websites.
privacyPageSharingDesc4: We respect your personal privacy when responding to access to information requests. We may have to release information (including personal information and commercial information) under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 and the Freedom of Information Act 2000; however we will only share where necessary to meet the statutory requirements of the legislation.
privacyPageSharingDesc5: We may also have to release information under the following legislation:
privacyPageSharingLi4: 2018 Data Protection legislation on the Isle of Man
privacyPageSharingLi5: The Data Protection (Bailiwick of Guernsey) Law, 2017
privacyPageSharingLi6: The Data Protection (Jersey) Law 2018 and the Data Protection Authority (Jersey) Law 2018
privacyPageSharingDesc6: We will only share your personal data where we are legally permitted to do so.
privacyPageRetentionHeading: How long we are keeping your personal data
privacyPageRetentionDesc1: Your personal data will be kept by us in line with our retention schedules to inform and support the aim of sustainable exploitation of UK commercial activities and the prevention of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
privacyPageRetentionDesc2: We shall hold and process personal data only for so long as is necessary for the fulfilment of the stated purpose or when legally required to do so. For example, as long as a vessel is in service as a fishing vessel we will retain records of current and previous owners in order to facilitate our work as a regulator. We review our policies regularly.
privacyPageRetentionDesc3: Your personal information will be processed and stored securely using appropriate technical and organisational measures.
privacyPageRetentionDesc4Suffix: for information on any potential exceptions.

privacyPageAutomatedHeading: Use of automated decision-making or profiling
privacyPageAutomatedDesc: The personal data you provide is not used for:
privacyPageAutomatedLi1: automated decision making (making a decision by automated means without any human involvement)
privacyPageAutomatedLi2: profiling (automated processing of personal data to evaluate certain things about an individual)
privacyPageNoDataHeading: What happens if you do not provide the personal data
privacyPageNoDataDesc: If you do not provide requested information, we will be unable to issue you with a UK export catch certificate, processing statement, or non-manipulation document, which could mean that you are unable to export your commodity and could result in further action being taken in-line with MMO’s compliance enforcement strategy.
privacyPageTransferHeading: Transfer of your personal data outside of the United Kingdom
privacyPageTransferDesc1: Where necessary, we may transfer personal information outside the UK to another country or Crown Dependency that is deemed adequate for data protection purposes. This means that the country or Crown Dependency has equivalent levels of data protection to that of the UK.
privacyPageTransferDesc2: This includes where we transfer data to the EU, for example when sharing data with the EU’s CATCH system.
privacyPageTransferDesc3: MMO may also in some circumstances transfer data to other countries without an adequacy agreement, having first taken all precautions to ensure that it was safe to do so, complying with the terms of the UK GDPR by making sure appropriate safeguards are in place.
privacyPageTransferDesc4: Where necessary, our data processors may share personal information outside of the UK. When doing so, they comply with the UK GDPR, making sure appropriate safeguards are in place. Personal information will only be transferred outside of the UK or EEA when necessary, lawful and complementary to our work carried out in the public interest, i.e. enforcement, or verification of documentation outside of the UK or EEA.

privacyPageRightsDesc2: Where such data relates to the possibility of a criminal offence, this data is further processed under Part 3 of the Data Protection Act 2018 (“The Act”) and your rights will be different.
